title: CREATE INDEX Statement
description: Learn how to create non-clustered indexes using the CREATE INDEX statement.

data.text: A nonclustered index is a data structure that improves the speed of data retrieval from tables. Unlike a clustered index, a nonclustered index sorts and stores data separately from the data rows in the table.

data.title: Basic CREATE INDEX Syntax
data.content: Creates a non-clustered index on a single column.

data.text: The NONCLUSTERED keyword is optional. You should place the columns that you often use to query data at the beginning of the column list.

data.title: Index on city column
data.content: Creates a non-clustered index for the city column to speed up queries.

data.title: Index on last_name and first_name
data.content: Creates a non-clustered index on multiple columns.
data.code:
CREATE INDEX ix_customers_name
ON sales.customers(last_name, first_name);

data.title: CREATE INDEX Key Points
points: A non-clustered index copies selected columns and stores them in a separate B-tree structure.
A table can have multiple non-clustered indexes.
Place frequently queried columns at the beginning of the column list.
Use CREATE INDEX to enhance query speed on filtered or joined columns.
